I farm in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so I will keep doing what fits my land, water, and labor best. I am 63, so I do not want a plan that is too complicated or too risky. I will mainly grow the usual wheat-maize rotation, because I know it well, it matches the local climate, and I can manage it with the machinery and habits I already have. Winter wheat uses the cold season and brings steady grain income, then summer maize follows right after harvest and makes full use of the heat and rain. I will use improved or hybrid seed because I want stable emergence, better disease resistance, and more reliable yield than old saved seed. I will control fertilizer instead of pushing too hard, because fertilizer is expensive and too much nitrogen can cause lodging and waste. I will irrigate a few key times, especially for wheat, since water matters most at the critical stages. I will use rotary tillage because it is practical for me and faster to manage across the year. I will spray pesticides only as needed for the common local pests and diseases, keeping the number moderate. This is the plan I would follow because it is steady, familiar, and realistic for my age, my experience, and local conditions.
